notes.title: Version 0.8.9b
notes.content:
Pushing to the main branch now -

Cooking improvements - you are allowed to have 1 oven per house and better ovens are available from Bob's store when you upgrade your house. Ovens cook food but it now takes time. You can queue up more items if you get a better oven. The value of meals has gone up to reflect the time it takes to make - so if a recipe takes 2 beets to make it should sell for more than the value of selling 2 beets. I'm considering adding quality levels to meals - any thoughts on that?

I'd like to make the refrigerator behave as a container for the oven recipes but that's for another update unfortunately. I currently am debating some of the ingredients that you just buy from Melody - I'd like to make the recipes a little simpler by removing those cheap ingredients you can simply buy in bulk from the store.

Removed fishing minigame - it's now just click and collect. The time you have to click is pretty relaxed now too. I want people to be able to zone out while fishing and relax and the quick time minigame is kind of the opposite of that. Overall I'm not sure fishing minigames really add a whole lot to these kinds of games. I'm on the fence about it. Perhaps a certain type of really well implemented minigame would be good but for now I'll just remove it. It also makes fishing faster so overall it's a buff to fishing.

Slightly increased movement speed and significantly increased swing speed. Swing speed is pretty fast now so enjoy it while it lasts...

Added some new wood furniture. Furniture is really lacking - sorry about that. Now you can make some basic chairs and a table so that's something. Maybe I'll try to add a few pieces each update.

The columns in the new mines have been shortened so you can see better in the mines (although it's pretty dark). Also there are pits now - but you can't fall in them. And the slimes come in different colors now. I made a slightly new boss but he's not quite in the game yet. I'm thinking of how he would get activated...do you have to find him wandering in the mines or perhaps there's an altar where you can summon him somehow...not sure yet. I think I need to look into how it's done in other games.

You can now use Esc to progress to the next dialogue and instantly skip the typewriter effect. This just saves an extra Esc key press so it's a little faster and cleaner. You can still press Esc and then click on Skip to skip most cutscenes.

Added the dynamic shadows to trees.

This update also comes with the new equip system but that's been on the beta branch for a couple weeks.

Probably some other little stuff but I'm not great at documenting everything.


About the mines -
It's been a lot of work to get the procedural generation working well and it still needs some work. Really, I'd like to get some better enemies in the mines but it's hard given the amount of animation required for each of them. I might sacrifice a little bit on the animations and artwork to get some more monsters out quickly. I think once I have this system done I can add 5 different tiers of mines the player can progress through along with the story and it will serve as a good framework for the game.

Anyways, sorry for breaking your saves again and I hope you enjoy the update. See ya next time.

notes.title: Nov 11 v0.8.9
notes.content:
Hi everyone. I've been working on an update and I've decided to push it to the beta branch since it will break current saves. I will continue working on it for a couple weeks until I push it to the default branch. 

There is no new story in this release but quite a few changes:

[list]
[*] New type of mines available. You can mine through walls in any direction (practically endlessly). I will be improving the random generation going forward. Hopefully I can add rivers and pits soon so it feels more alive and adventurous but I think it's already pretty neat as it is. Let me know what you think.

[*] New equip system - you can equip armor and trinkets on your character. I added a few simple sets of armor for now and a trinket that provides some lighting in the mines. Also, you can optionally equip swords and they will show up in the toolbar so you don't have to arrange your inventory. There's a new hotkey to quick switch to your equipped sword (R).

[*] Some new items and things to craft. Generally fixed a bunch of bugs. Wispy will assist you in the mines. The furnace is now a stone furnace with nicer lighting - hoping to add different types of furnaces in the future and probably a tiered workbench system. Cooking will probably change but that's for another update. Villidium ore renamed to Twilight ore because it sounds cooler imo.

[*] You can move while using tools and swinging swords now. It generally makes the game easier to play and less tedious. I really wanted to be able to hold a direction while mining so now you can.

[/list]

Will probably remove the fishing minigame completely so speak now if you really want it to stay in the game.

Thanks for playing and I appreciate any feedback I get.

Once you've placed it on your farm, you can place items inside in order to make them available for sale to visitors. You can enable visitors by using the sign at the entrance to your farm. Visitors will come and browse your goods, and buy one item (if there is one available). These items sell for approximately double the shipped price. notes.title: Wholesome Games Festival and MoS Update 0.8.8.0
notes.content:
Hi everyone. Melody of Seasons will be participating in the Wholesome Games Festival tomorrow and it has received a brand new update so that any new players can have the most up to date experience!

This update includes some neat things including a new area called The Great Marsh. This new area is inhabited by a few lonely humanoids called Sporefolk. You'll have to gather Marsh Essence from daily quests and donate to increase your Renown level with them. There are five renown levels and with each level you'll be able to get better rewards from the Marsh. As I just mentioned there is a new mine in this area that has a lot of Iron nodes. This mine has no floors, but it does have worker wisps that will help you mine a little faster. As you gain Renown level you'll get more wisps that will help you in the mine.

There's also a new combat and foraging area called the Endless Mire where you can fight some new monsters and forage for items. [b]Oh, and btw if you get to Renown Level 2 you can fast travel to and from the Marsh with a giant frog![/b]

Ok so now the slightly bad news - I really wanted to have the entire Marsh area completed in time for the Wholesome Festival tomorrow but unfortunately I couldn't finish it. Currently, gaining Renown with the Sporefolk will not progress the story further. I need to add more quests and add more story beats to the Marsh to make it more special and interesting. It's frustrating to me because it feels like everything is always 'almost' complete but not quite. Everything can always be improved and it's hard for me to move on sometimes.

Anyways, maybe you can see where the game is going with this latest update. I think adding new areas with Renown tiers will add to the sense of progression in the game. I'll probably redo the old mines to be similar to what the Iron Mines are - just one room with some automated mining helpers. I don't think having 100 floors of mining floors really adds much to the game. Having a system like this where each new area has a new tier of ores rather than all ores being accessible from the start gives a better sense of progression.

This may come as a shock to some of you but I have a confession to make - I never finished Stardew Valley. I got to the point where my farm was getting rather large and when I got up in the morning I just looked at all the stuff I had to do and I just gave up. So I'd like to add more automation to the game. I am thinking about adding wisps that will harvest, water, and do all kinds of work on your farm.

I'm still focusing on finishing the Marsh, but for the future areas I want to do more different things to keep the gameplay fresh so that it's not just a simple reskin of the previous area. That might take more time so we'll see how it goes. Besides taking the game in a 'Stranger' ... direction I'm not sure where I'm going with it. Stay tuned and find out!

Thanks for playing, and see you in the next update.

notes.title: June 6 Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone, sorry for the delay - things took a lot longer than I expected and there were a lot of bugs to work through.

***This update will again break your old save files. If you want to keep you save file, don't update. I feel bad about breaking people's saves but I think it has to be done at this point so I can make faster progress with the game. If you do update, you can always go back to a previous version of the game using Steam.

Some of the new things in this update:

[list]
[*] Improved the story line, new cutscenes, new intro and a new event.
[*] Skill system revamp - 50 levels for each skill and faster leveling in the beginning.
[*] Skill gains increased, but skill gains are random now (most actions are now a 50/50 chance to trigger)
[*] Talents! New talents for each skill. You'll gain 1 talent point to spend every other level up.
[*] Foraging renamed to Trailblazing as it includes movement abilities and social skill abilities.
[*] Combat Skill added!
[*] You can now track NPC wish lists with the quest system. Just check the "Track" toggle when you open the wish list.
[/list]

Generally I want to let you know the game is moving towards a more "traditional" RPG style. I've seen a lot of super cozy games coming out lately and while my game will still have a lot of cozy elements, I'm just going to do my own thing from now on. If I learned one thing from early access it's that people want something different and unique so I'm working towards that. I think there are a lot of interesting things that could be done on top of the farming-sim base, but most games don't really explore them because just making a "basic" farming-sim game takes a long time.

Well, that's all for now. Let me know if you have any questions or comments! See you in the next update.

notes.title: May 28 - MoS update
notes.content:
Hi everyone, just wanted to give an announcement since it's been over a week since the last update.

I am currently finishing a big update and hope to have it done by the end of the week. I totally revamped the skill system and added the Combat skill. Each skill will have 50 levels now and you'll get a talent point to spend every other level. So there will be talents now for each skill. I hope this adds to a feeling of progression and gives more visibility into how you're progressing. Since there are 50 levels, you'll gain levels faster in the beginning and feel like you're making a lot of progress early on. Of course, the levels will take more and more experience as you level up. I'll hope for your feedback if it's too fast or slow. There will be a lot of balance tweaks I'm sure.

I am also improving the introduction and initial quest line. I want the start of the game to feel more interesting and streamlined. The game is pretty solid in terms of gameplay but I need to work more on the world-building and story of the game. There needs to be a more interesting story line for the game. I want new players to be able to get into the game, follow along the main quest line and experience a full story. I'm getting there, but I keep getting sucked into doing more and more gameplay stuff (like talent trees and other quality of life improvements). In any good RPG, you play through the main quest line and at the end you look back at your achievements and how far you've come and think "wow, what an experience it was". That's my goal for this game. A more immersive story is a must IMO.

Anyways, those are my thoughts for now, hope to see an update near the end of the week or maybe later. See you in the next update.

notes.title: Melody of Seasons v0.8.6.3
notes.content:
Hi everyone, I'm releasing an update a little early this week. Here's what's in it:

[list]
[*] Quest Rewards and UI - A new reward UI pop up for quest rewards with bonus choices.
[*] Skill Bar HUD - When you gain a skill it shows up in a progress bar on the left side of the screen so you can better see how far you're progressed within the level. The old way of notifying with text is turned off now.
[*] Zoom buttons - added zoom buttons for the camera. Only works in outdoor scenes. The buttons are located in the date time display in the top left portion of the screen.
[*] Improvements to Bulletin Board quests - they now show the item status in the HUD.
[*] Quests should all update properly in the HUD now.
[*] Added a couple items that drop from slimes and bats that could be useful in the future, for now they can just be sold.
[*] Monsters can drop gold now.
[*] Quest log will select the first quest when opened.

notes.title: Jan23 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Hi everyone. I've decided to release the next build!

[b]**Old save files will no longer work with this build! (sorry)***[/b]

First and foremost I want to note that the combat system (or lake thereof) is nowhere near complete. Since it will take some time to fully flesh out the combat, I didn't want to hold up all the other changes I've been working on. I have some plans to make combat more interesting and will release more details in the future.

Here's what's included with this patch:

[b]Item quality levels[/b]: There are 5 levels of quality for crops and foraged items. Currently, the quality you receive is based on your farming or foraging skill. There are still no quality levels for fish but maybe in the future there will be. The sell value of these goods has been decreased significantly for lower quality levels so money may be harder to come by in the early game. Every step up in quality is a 15% increase in the sell value of the crops.

[b]Fertilizers[/b]: There are 3 fertilizers in the game now. Water Sipper Fertilizer which causes tiles to retain water so you only have to water once for the lifetime of the crop. Weed Ward Fertilizer which will prevent weeds from growing on the crop. And High Yield Fertilizer which will give you a chance to double your harvest output. Fertilizers can be bought from Melody in any season. They can only be applied on tilled soil or tilled soil with seeds. Once the crop has grown a single day, you will no longer be able to add fertilizer. The type of fertilizer will show up in the crop tooltip when you hover over so you'll know what fertilizer your crops have. There may be more fertilizers in the future.

[b]Combat[/b]: There is a new area in the mines with monsters. If you want to avoid combat you can still use the old mines as they were. The sword 'tool' has been changed to the sickle. There are 3 new types of swords that can be bought from Melody that simply do increasing amounts of damage. You'll have to carry these in your inventory and use them like a regular item if you want to do more damage. If you finish the tutorial, wispy will accompany you in the slime-infested mines and he will shoot projectiles at the enemies. I will be exploring adding companions to the game as well as stats for your companions and yourself. Also hopefully I'll be adding rare swords and equipment for combat as well. And more dungeons in the future. Currently the slime mines are simply another way to mine ore but that will change later. Also, with combat I've added health. So now there is a health and energy for your player. If your health or hp drops to 0 you will pass out and wake up the next morning with your energy diminished.

[b]Beach Shack[/b]: You can buy the beach shack and sleep there if you like. Just interact with the sign in order to purchase it (if you're rich enough). If you sleep there, you'll wake up there the next day of course. You can hear the waves from inside which is cool too.

[b]A map[/b]: The map tab is added to the Menu UI (hotkey m). Each tile represents a scene. There's a star that indicates where you are currently. When you hover over the tile, some details about the scene are shown along with the NPCs that should be in the scene at the current time. The map doesn't drill into each and every scene. For example, if an NPC is in their house, they will be shown to be in the Town scene (or whatever scene their house is located in). The map is a little crude but I hope it is effective enough for now.

Also: Many other bug fixes and improvements. Probably some other things I'm forgetting to mention at the moment.

Let me know if you encounter any bugs!

notes.title: Melody of Seasons Update
notes.content:
Hi everyone. I hope you had a nice New Years and Holidays.

I wanted to make a quick update about the game. First of all, I'm sorry for the lack of updates. My motivation tends to ebb and flow, sometimes I have extreme energy to make progress and other times quite the opposite. That's just always been the way I operate and I wish I could always be "on" but I guess that's just not me.

I had been working on adding combat into the game which was taking a bit longer than expected and in the meantime I couldn't resist adding some other features like fertilizers and crop quality levels, and a map. Then I started refactoring a bunch of code that was bothering me. Well now I've got to a point where it looks like old save files will not be compatible with the new version of the game. I could perhaps work on making them compatible but I'm not sure it's worth it. There's a good chance you'll have to start over if you update to the new version. This may be a risk in the future as well so I think I'll try to make bigger but less frequent updates so as not to annoy people too much. It will allow me to make progress more quickly if I don't have to worry about breaking older save files, but it comes at the cost of potentially annoying the players since their old save files will not load.

Anyways I'd also like to try adding a robust quest system before the next update since that's an area I really would like to improve. If I can add quests more easily I think the game will feel a lot nicer and it will give the player a lot more clear direction in terms of what to do next in the game. Currently, there is a quest system but it's a bit of a hot mess from a developer point of view. Adding quests is painful and because of that, there aren't enough of them. I'd like to have a main story quest and side quests as well as the ability to track certain tasks like wish lists.

I keep pushing the story elements out but hopefully I'll get to that in the future. I'm not sure when I'll get the next update out - maybe in a month or so. I'm not sure. I'm not great at planning these kinds of things.

Well, I hope you're doing okay out there and thanks for playing my little game.

Hi everyone, I pushed a new build that includes some important new changes and bug fixes

[list]
[*] Added two new scenes - West Town and The Boardwalk

[/list]

I added some new little minigames or daily quests for Valerie. I will be working on her heart cutscenes next (she's the only NPC besides Joe without cutscenes at this point). I would like to add daily quests and little mini-games for each NPC so that you're not just giving them gifts repeatedly in order to increase your heart level - it should be more fun than that! Each day, you can get a daily quest from Valerie's house that is a simple task you can complete to get +4 heart points with Valerie.

I also decided to move Fleur's house to West Town because I think it feels better there. Let me know what you think of the new changes! The West Town scene contains Fleur's House and Valerie's House. It has a lot of ponds you can fish from and is a good spot for Morel foraging. The Boardwalk can be reached by exiting the Town to the south or from the east side of the beach.

Right now, I think I need to focus on improving the character stories as well as creating an interesting over-arching story. I'm hoping to add some more fantastical elements, but it's taking some time. Creating cutscenes is hard for me but I'm doing my best. I'm also looking into getting some new portrait artwork. notes.title: What's next for Melody of Seasons?
notes.content:
Hi everyone, I just wanted to give an update on the progress I've been making with the game.

Lately I've been making a [i]ton[/i] of progress and it feels great. I've been working on this game on and off for a very long time and now that I can see the it coming together I am more motivated than ever. There are just a few more things I'd like to get in the game and then I can consider releasing it into early access.

There is some conventional wisdom that one should participate in Steam Next Fest before releasing in order to build wishlists but the next one is in February and I think I may be able to release well before then. If all goes well, I'll get the game into a good state within a month, and take some time to thoroughly playtest it to make sure there aren't many issues on release. I think if I learned anything from the demo release, it's that there will always be issues and I'll just have to work on them post-release. Especially as a solo developer there's just no way I can find and fix every bug that's possible and perfectly 'one-shot' the release.

So my plans are to finish the last few features of the game: 

[list]
[*] Upgrading your house to the final level.
[*] A winter festival.
[*] More achievements.
[*] More player customization options.
[*] An area where you can harvest wood and greens besides the farm.
[*] Some UI improvements.
[*] Other quality of life improvements.
[/list]

There are more areas that I'd like to improve but they can be done in early access such as improving the story, perhaps a better quest system, and improved character portraits among other things.

I'll also update the demo one more time so it gets all the latest improvements. I plan on keeping the demo up forever. Not many people have played the demo but it looks like some people have played for a considerable amount of time and that's amazing.

I have so many cool ideas I'd like to add to the game but it all depends on [i]releasing the game[/i]. It's really important to me that people are playing and enjoying the game. I can have all the neat ideas in the world but if the game never gets released it doesn't matter!

So keep an eye out for a release date and thank you so much for playing!

notes.title: Demo v0.3.0 released
notes.content:
*** NOTE: YOU MUST START A NEW SAVE FILE IF YOU UPDATE ***

Hello everyone. I just released version 0.3.0 which includes some big improvements to the Foraging skill. Here's a summary of the main changes.

[list]
[*] Added the Bird Bath craftable item learned from Foraging level 2. It can be placed on the farm to attract different birds which can drop valuable feathers when you scare them off. The bird bath must be filled with water to attract birds. Every day there is a chance to attract 1 bird per bird bath. Water will last a few days in spring and fall but only a day or two during the hot summer. Does not function during winter. When there is a bird at the bird bath it will cause water to splash which can water nearby crops. You can refill the bird bath water with your watering can or it will fill during a rain.
[*] Added Foraging skill buffs. Every Foraging level will grant a new Foraging ability buff. For example when foraging you can get a speed buff that stacks so if you forage a few items in a row without losing the buff, you can get moving pretty quick. Another buff that is available will grant energy every so often that also stacks and lasts a longer period of time.
[*] Added some mushrooms to forage. Morel mushrooms will be abundant after a rainy day.
[*] Concrete Mixers can now be placed on the farm. The recipe is learned on Mining level 2.
[*] Adjusted some recipe numbers and item values.
[*] Added squirrels which can drop various nuts when scared away - can also grant Foraging skill up
[*] Added seagulls that can also be scared away causing some random items to drop
[*] Lots of other bug fixes
[/list]

Thank you for playing!
